clue.text: Fantastic score sure is capital!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly imagined, telling us to rework the letters of the two words beside it

explanation.surface: An excited cry that a great result is simply capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'Fantastic' reshuffles SCORE and SURE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital in the financial sense is wealth or assets, the stock of means a business can draw on.

clue.text: Urchin seen to play the fool with a tea-cake

parts.note: to rag is to indulge in boisterous horseplay or pranks
taken as written
a muffin is a flat bread cake eaten toasted at teatime

explanation.surface: A street child is spotted clowning about with a tea-cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a ragged, scruffy child, which is just what the old word for a ragged waif describes.

clue.text: Whisky soda drink — one with bite!

explanation.surface: A whisky and soda is a drink with a real kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a cocktail name, here a whisky and soda; and literally it is anything that stings, such as a wasp.

clue.text: Cauterises these internal organs, in hospital patients

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the word Cauterises, ready to be lifted out

explanation.surface: A surgeon cauterises wombs during operations on hospital patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' and 'hospital patients' are surface padding: the organs are found in the word Cauterises.
explanation.definitionFit: These are wombs, the plural of the Latin word for the internal organ that carries a foetus.

clue.text: Riders receiving applause when containing a disturbance

indicators.note: containing says the word for applause holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: cheers are shouts of applause
taken as written
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: Horsemen are cheered as they quell an outbreak of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' and 'when' are link words; 'Riders' suggests horsemen, but these drove chariots.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers were the drivers who rode in chariots, as in Roman races.

clue.text: Money to the value of three quarters?

parts.note: south is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated to its initial
east is another compass quarter, shortened to its initial
north is a third compass quarter, shortened to its initial

explanation.surface: A question about how much cash makes up seventy-five per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters' looks like a fraction but means three compass points; 'to the value of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sen is a small coin, a hundredth of the Japanese yen and of some other Asian currencies.

clue.text: Sacked and sent up in flames

explanation.surface: Someone lost their job and their workplace went up in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dismissed from a job is to be let go; and something set alight has been burnt.

clue.text: Get stoned!

parts.note: reads like an invitation to drugs or a biblical punishment, but means to turn literally into stone over the ages, as ancient remains do

explanation.surface: An exhortation to get high.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic remains preserved in rock gradually become petrified, turning into rock themselves.

clue.text: Gives way though soldier gets direction to hold fast

indicators.note: to hold says the first pieces grip the word for fast between them

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords
S, south, is a compass direction
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone yields although a soldier is ordered to stand firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' and 'gets' are link words; 'hold fast' reads as one phrase meaning grip firmly, but 'fast' is the Lenten fast. RE (Royal Engineers) is a standard crossword soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give in after resisting.

clue.text: Periods of bewilderment, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us to take the sound of the word for bewilderment, not its spelling

parts.note: a daze is a state of stunned bewilderment

explanation.surface: Times when one feels confused, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of time, as in 'those were the days', are periods.

clue.text: A semblance to the chaps, say?

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the word for the chaps is pronounced

parts.note: guys is an informal word for men or chaps

explanation.surface: A question about how something appears to a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or pretence, a semblance of something.

clue.text: Shy member of the family?

parts.note: suggests a timid relative, but shy means a throw, as at a fairground where balls are hurled at a figure called by a family title and a woman's name

explanation.surface: A bashful relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground and pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy's head; the name also means a target of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in the game is named like a relative and is the thing thrown at, so a shy target that sounds like kin.

clue.text: Noticing mafia involvement in blowing up

indicators.note: involvement suggests things tangled together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Spotting that organised crime was behind an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'blowing up' looks like an explosion but means enlarging an image.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarging something, as with a lens or photographic enlargement, is making it bigger.

clue.text: Tentatively moving and thus concentrating

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the word before it are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Going forward hesitantly and so focusing hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; the definition 'thus concentrating' means in a focused manner, matching the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with close focus and care is to do it in a concentrating, heedful way.

clue.text: Pretends to be changing spare notes

indicators.note: changing tells us to alter the order of the letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A con artist poses as someone while swapping spare banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: To impersonate someone is to assume their identity, which is to pose as them.

clue.text: Inside workers fret about outside agitation

indicators.note: Inside places the workers within the other piece
outside confirms the rearranged letters surround the workers
about signals that the letters of fret are turned around into a new arrangement

parts.note: men are workers, as in a workforce

explanation.surface: Staff indoors worry about unrest outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of fret to FERT, which then wraps around the workers; 'Inside' and 'outside' both describe the one container.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferment is a state of unrest or turmoil, as in political upheaval.

clue.text: Emergence of, for example, last actor — with noises off

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of the Latin for 'for example'

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word actor
off signals the letters of noises are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A stage direction about the last performer leaving, with sound effects from the wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'with' are link words; 'off' makes ESSION from NOISES. 'Noises off' is a theatre term for offstage sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming out or going forth, as an exit, is a way of emerging.

clue.text: Sad without even opening the port

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the word for sad goes around the other letter

parts.note: triste is a literary word, from French, for sad

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of even

explanation.surface: Feeling down without even beginning the harbour visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major Adriatic seaport in north-east Italy.

clue.text: Recruited for the police in large numbers

explanation.surface: Lots of people signed up to join the constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins the police is in the Force; and a crowd turning out en masse comes in great strength.

clue.text: Provide what may be sole container for container

indicators.note: container for says the fish surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a sole is one example of a fish
an urn is a vessel or container

explanation.surface: Supplying a box for footwear, the sole sort of container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what may be sole' defines by example, a sole being one kind of fish; the second 'container' is the piece placed within.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with something is to supply or equip them with it.

clue.text: Is annoying in a way that's mainly unnecessary

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: needless means not needed

explanation.surface: Something irritates because it is largely superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way that's' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad or provoke someone with jibes is to irritate them persistently.

clue.text: Hangs around, upsetting toilers

indicators.note: upsetting suggests knocking over and disturbing, so the letters of toilers are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone idles about, annoying the hard workers.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or linger aimlessly in one place is to idle about.

clue.text: It's not a cruise arranged for freeing the airways

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the preceding words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: It isn't a planned voyage that frees up the airways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'airways' looks like air travel to go with the cruise, but means the breathing passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviving someone who has stopped breathing includes clearing their breathing passages, as in first aid.

clue.text: Quite in order to be executed? How gruesome!

indicators.note: to be executed means losing the head, so the first letter is chopped off

parts.note: lawful means permitted, entirely in order

explanation.surface: Is it legitimate to put someone to death? What a horror!
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful or terrible things prompt the exclamation of disgust.

clue.text: Star seen when the river's rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the Avon is a familiar English river, Shakespeare's at Stratford

explanation.surface: A celestial object visible when the water level goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen when the' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness.

clue.text: Launch — otherwise I get in a train

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or else'

indicators.note: train in the sense of shaping or directing tells us to reorder the letters before it

explanation.surface: Set off, or else I board a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train', in the sense of shaping or guiding, reshuffles the letters of I GET IN A, giving IGINATE; the surface makes it a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a venture is to start it off or bring it into being.

clue.text: Radio music

explanation.surface: Broadcast melodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting is being on the airwaves; and a tune or melody is also an aria-like song.

clue.text: Squadron that's flying?

explanation.surface: A group of aircraft in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval squadron or group of ships is a navy unit; and swift, rapid motion is described with this adjective.

clue.text: White, like a Rhode island red?

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a Rhode Island Red is a breed of chicken, here a female bird

explanation.surface: A question whether something pale resembles a chicken of a reddish breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets white against red, but the Rhode Island Red is just a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey-white or pale, the colour of ash, as of a frightened face.

clue.text: Extreme reactionaries, of solitary disposition and single

indicators.note: disposition in the sense of arrangement says the letters of solitary are laid out afresh

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for single, as in personal ads

explanation.surface: Hardline conservatives of a lonely temperament and unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'and' are link words; 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the monarchy are traditionalists, so the term is applied to staunch conservatives.
